SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 5535
Date 19 / 12 / 33

December 19 33.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of your
letter No.3657 of December 8,1933, regarding one Chin
Shih Hou(陈世侯), and to inform you that enquiries have
failed so far to locate him. Chin taught and resided at
the Chen Siu(慎修) School, No.1 Tai Chong Li, Jukong Road,
Chapel, during September and October 1933, and left for
an unknown destination at the end of October. Ex-officials
of the now defunct World Overseas Chinese Federation, No.128
Kweichow Road, who were interviewed, state that Chin Shih Hou
was only an ordinary member of the Federation and never took
any part in its activities. Consequently his movements
are unknown to them.

Further enquiries are being continued and should
Chin Shih Hou be located, the information will be duly
passed to you.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
〔签名〕
Officer i/c Special Branch.

J. Van den Berg, Esq.,
Netherlands Consulate-General.

〔左下角签名〕

1933年12月19日。

先生：

谨此确认收到您1933年12月8日关于陈世侯（Chin Shih Hou，陈世侯）的第3657号来信，并告知您，截至目前，调查未能找到其下落。陈于1933年9月和10月期间在闸北虬江路泰忠里1号慎修学校任教并居住，于10月底前往未知目的地。经询问现已解散的世界华侨联合会（地址：贵州路128号）的前官员，他们表示陈世侯仅是该会的普通成员，从未参与其任何活动。因此，他们不知晓其行踪。

进一步调查正在进行中，若找到陈世侯，将及时向您通报相关信息。

此致
敬礼

〔签名〕
特别股主管警官。

J. Van den Berg 先生，
荷兰总领事馆。

〔左下角签名〕

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. File No. D 5535 Date 21/12/33）
S. ____
Date December 18, 1933

Subject (in full) Enquiry from local Netherlands Consulate-General
re whereabouts of one Chin Shih Hou (陳士侯).

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by Whounean O.S.

With reference to the endorsement of the
Officer i/c Special Branch appearing on the attached
letter, dated December 8, 1933, from the local Netherlands
Consulate-General requesting information as to the present
whereabouts of one Chin Shih Hou (陳士侯), I have to report
that enquiries elicit that following an arrangement made
by Chin Sing Nyi (陳心義), a teacher at the Chen Siu (慎修)
School, No.1 Tai Chong Li (泰白里), Jukong Road, Chapei,
Chin Shih Hou taught and resided at this school during
September and October, 1933. At the end of the latter
month, Chin Sing Nyi resigned his position in the above
institution, whereupon Chin Shih Hou departed for an
unknown destination.

Enquiries made from the ex-operators of the now
defunct World Overseas Chinese Federation, No.128 Kweichow
Road, indicate that as Chin Shih Hou was only an ordinary
member of that organization and never took part in any of its
routine work or activities nothing was known of his private
affairs, and consequently his present whereabouts were not
known.

D. S. Pitts
D. S.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

（批：This matter will be kept in touch with and should information be received as to the whereabouts of Chin Shih-hou a report will be submitted.
Wh 18 12/33.）

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 刑事及特别股登记处。档案号 D 5535 日期 33年12月21日）
S. ____
日期 1933年12月18日

主题（全称） 本地荷兰总领事馆关于查询陈士侯（Chin Shih Hou，陳士侯）下落的问询。

由 D.S. Pitts 制作，由 Whounean O.S. 转呈。

鉴于附函（日期为1933年12月8日，来自本地荷兰总领事馆）上特别股主管警官的批注，该函要求提供陈士侯（Chin Shih Hou，陳士侯）目前的下落，兹报告如下：经查询获悉，根据闸北虬江路泰白里1号慎修学校教师陈心义（Chin Sing Nyi，陳心義）的安排，陈士侯于1933年9月和10月期间在该校任教并居住。当月月底，陈心义辞去了在上述机构的职务，随后陈士侯前往未知目的地。

向现已解散的世界华侨联合会（地址：贵州路128号）的前经办人员进行的查询表明，由于陈士侯仅是该组织的普通成员，从未参与其任何日常工作或活动，故无人知晓其私事，因此也不知其目前下落。

D. S. Pitts
D. S.
特别股主管警官。

（批注：此事将持续跟进，若收到关于陈世侯下落的信息，将提交报告。
Wh 18 12/33。）

C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 5535
Date 12 / 12 / 33

SHANGHAI, 8 December 1933

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that the Netherlands
subject Jong Ngim-hoy (楊任海), born at Soengeiliat, Banka,
28 February 1914, holder of a Netherlands passport issued at
Pangkalpinang on 14 March 1933, No. 35, came to my office to
ask financial assistance.

It appears that when he was in Netherlands India one
of his friends, the Netherlands subject Chen Mou-chung alias
Tjhin Mow Tjhioeng (陳茂聰), born at Soengeiliat, Banka,
16 November 1915, holder of a "Verklaring van Ingezetenschap"
(Declaration of Residency), issued at Pangkalpinang on 6
March 1933, No. 49, induced him to go with him to Shanghai
for the purpose of study. Chen stated that he had an uncle
there, called Chin Shih-hou (陳世豪), who was well known
in educational circles and who would be able to offer Jong
a scholarship.

They arrived both at Shanghai on 10 April 1933 and
registered the same day at this Consulate General.

They stayed one night at the Sun Sun Hotel and after
that went to Chenju where they stayed for about a week with
a certain Lu Tung-chuan (盧東泉), only to find out that
the uncle, who at that time was teaching in a school on
Yukong Road (虬江路) Tai Chong Lee (泰昌里), (Chen Hsiu
School 慎修學校 ) was not in a position to assist them.
On the contrary it appears that he borrowed from Jong the
only money that was left to him, namely Sh.$ 15.-, Hongk.$ 1.-
and Neth.Fl. 7.50, besides an empty leather bag and a foun-
tain pen. Neither the money nor the borrowed articles were
ever returned.

T. P. Givens, Esquire,
Officer i/c Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

上海，1933年12月8日

先生：

谨此告知，荷兰籍臣民杨任海（Jong Ngim-hoy，楊任海），1914年2月28日出生于邦加岛双溪利亚特（Soengeiliat, Banka），持有1933年3月14日在邦加槟榔屿（Pangkalpinang）签发的第35号荷兰护照，前来我馆寻求经济援助。

据悉，当他在荷属东印度时，他的朋友之一、荷兰籍臣民陈茂聪（Chen Mou-chung，别名 Tjhin Mow Tjhioeng，陳茂聰），1915年11月16日出生于邦加岛双溪利亚特，持有1933年3月6日在邦加槟榔屿签发的第49号“居住声明”（Verklaring van Ingezetenschap），诱使他一同前往上海求学。陈声称他在那里有一位叔叔，名叫陈世豪（Chin Shih-hou，陳世豪），在教育界颇有名气，能够为杨提供奖学金。

两人于1933年4月10日抵达上海，并于同日在本总领事馆登记。

他们在孙孙旅馆（Sun Sun Hotel）住了一晚，随后前往陈州（Chenju，音译），在一位名叫卢东泉（Lu Tung-chuan，盧東泉）的人家中住了约一周，结果发现那位当时在虬江路泰昌里慎修学校任教的叔叔无力帮助他们。相反，据悉他还向杨借走了其仅剩的钱款，即上海银元15元、港币1元和荷兰盾7.50弗罗林，此外还有一个空皮包和一支钢笔。钱款和借用的物品均未归还。

T. P. Givens 先生，
特别股主管警官，
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。

Being

Being thus left stranded the two boys found a refuge in
the Cantonese Work Shelter (廣東工藝社) at Nin-kuei Road No.
237 (吟桂路), Chapei.

Jong in the meantime got into touch with his friends
in Netherlands India and was promised a position with "JAN"
& Co., Sigaren- en Tabakhandel at Bandoeng, Java, and part
of his passage money was advanced by this Consulate General,
so that he could leave on 7 December 1933 by the "Tjibadak"
for Soerabaia.

I enclose herewith two notes written by the uncle, from
which you will see that he states to be connected with the
World Federation of Chinese Colonists (全球華僑總公會),
the last known address of which was at 567 Nanking Road,
Shanghai.

I would be much obliged if investigations could be made
and Chin Shih-hou be located so that I can endeavour to
reclaim from him the money due to Jong. I do not know whe-
ther there is sufficient evidence to prosecute Chin Shih-hou,
the complainant having left Shanghai, whereas the nephew
Chen Mou-chung, who expects to receive sufficient money in
the near future to take up his studies, might not be willing
to testify against him.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

〔签名〕

Chinese Secretary.

（左侧手写批注：World Overseas Chinese Association / 8 Nanking Road）

SI,
For inquiry and report
please.
JHS
DEC 1 1 1933

-2-

因此陷入困境的两名少年在闸北吟桂路237号的广东工艺社找到了栖身之所。

与此同时，杨与他在荷属东印度的朋友取得了联系，并获承诺将在爪哇万隆的“JAN” & Co. 雪茄烟草贸易公司获得一个职位，本总领事馆预支了其部分路费，使他得以于1933年12月7日乘坐“Tjibadak”号轮船前往泗水（Soerabaia）。

随函附上两份由该叔叔写的便条，从中可见他声称与全球华侨总公会有关联，该会最后的已知地址为上海南京路567号。

如能进行调查并找到陈世豪，以便我设法向他追回欠杨的款项，我将不胜感激。我不确定是否有足够的证据起诉陈世豪，因为投诉人已离开上海，而其侄子陈茂聪预计不久后将收到足够资金以继续学业，可能不愿作证指控他。

此致
敬礼

〔签名〕

华务秘书。

（左侧手写批注：世界华侨协会 / 南京路8号）

SI，
请调查并报告。
JHS
1933年12月11日

Your woolen cloth I will take back from my friend there.
I look you just same my brother , So you must belive me any thing .
and I hope you and Mou Chung must lovely ,in the same time you and
Mou Chung must study hard . Your future will glorous !
Good - bye !
Your Loving Brother
Johnnchen

我收到了茂聪给我的你的钢笔和铅笔。我会保管好你的钢笔和铅笔。不用担心。
非常感谢！
你的毛料衣服我会从那里的朋友那里取回。
我看你就像我的亲兄弟一样，所以你必须相信我说的一切。
我希望你和茂聪和睦相处，同时你们必须努力学习。你们的未来将是光明的！
再见！
爱你的兄弟
Johnnchen
